# Raja Karthik Palakurthi — public portfolio summary

Raja Karthik Palakurthi is a Research Engineer and founding member of ZenteiQ.ai. His interests include language models, AI systems, evaluation, and reliable software. Former Project Associate at AiREX Lab, IISc.

Professional LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/palakurthirajakarthik/
Company: https://zenteiq.ai/
IISc AiREX Lab alumni: https://airexlab.cds.iisc.ac.in/alumni/

## Areas of focus

### Inference and performance

Engineering considerations behind responsive and dependable language-model applications.

Running a language model involves a series of practical tradeoffs. Responsiveness, resource use, and reliability all matter to the experience of using it.
I am interested in the fundamentals of inference performance and in how to reason about bottlenecks using reproducible, publicly discussable experiments.

- Latency and throughput as engineering concepts
- Measuring responsiveness under changing workloads
- Resource efficiency and the user experience
- Clear measurement, repeatability, and communication

Details: https://rajakarthik.com/work/inference-systems/

### Language model evaluation

Understanding instruction following, multilingual behavior, and where model outputs fall short.

A single benchmark score never tells the whole story. Evaluation also means examining consistency, instruction following, and the ways models fail on ordinary tasks.
I am interested in test design, qualitative error analysis, and comparing model behavior across different languages and task types.

- Instruction-following and response consistency
- Multilingual evaluation principles
- Error analysis and transparent reporting
- Reproducibility and careful interpretation

Details: https://rajakarthik.com/work/foundation-models/

### Agent reliability

Practical questions about tool use, recoverable workflows, and human oversight.

When software can make decisions and call tools, the difficult questions often concern boundaries: what it can do, what it should ask, and how it should recover.
I am interested in safe tool interaction, explicit state, meaningful human control, and evaluations that capture real task outcomes.

- Tool selection and clear permissions
- Recovery from errors and interruptions
- Human review at meaningful decision points
- Testing behavior across longer interactions

Details: https://rajakarthik.com/work/agent-runtimes/

### Context and retrieval

How assistants find relevant information without losing provenance or user control.

More context does not automatically make an answer better. The challenge is selecting relevant information, interpreting it carefully, and knowing when uncertainty remains.
My interests include information retrieval, source attribution, changing information, and evaluating whether retrieved context actually helps.

- Relevance and source attribution
- Handling stale or conflicting information
- Precision versus completeness in retrieval
- User control and sensible uncertainty

Details: https://rajakarthik.com/work/memory-retrieval/

### Reliable AI services

Software engineering principles for clear, observable, and maintainable AI applications.

A useful AI application is more than the model behind it. Clear interfaces, predictable behavior, and careful failure handling make the difference for the people using it.
I am interested in the software engineering principles that make AI-backed services easier to test, operate, and improve.

- Clear interfaces and error handling
- Observability as a general engineering practice
- Performance and reliability tradeoffs
- Maintainable software and testing discipline

Details: https://rajakarthik.com/work/api-platform/
